title: Trombonist Baron Morehead and his Club Alabam band
summary: Lee describes Baron Morehead as a short, older trombonist-bandleader who kept good musicians and a good book at the Alabam.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So we're just about back up to your time, I think, with Nat. Oh, you mentioned Baron [Morehead's] band. What band was that? Tell me about him.

Oh yeah. Baron Morehead was a little trombone player; he must have been about 5 foot 3, and he was a trombonist. And he was an older man, you know, but the older guys were more business and they could get most of the gigs in Los Angeles, because they could keep the bands together and they would always show up, you know. I imagine it was the same way all over.

Yeah, he always -- it's a funny thing -- the guys were always smart enough; they would always hire the good musicians because they kept the better jobs, and he always kept a good book, and you know, when you're coming up, you always want to play some good music, and so he had a good book. Yeah, he was at the Alabam for a long time. Of course, he and Curtis Mosby were very, very

good friends, you know? I think the last time I worked with Baron Morehead at the Club Alabam for Curtis Mosby, that was the time -- it seems that I told you -- that maybe I did, maybe I didn't --that they had to pay me before I went -- before I started playing every night? Well, that was his band, and also Baron Morehead's band.
